text:
leah: after upgrading to redwoodctl 0.13.2 on macbook pro (arm), `redwoodctl login --sso` opens a browser but the CLI prints: 
```
> login complete
failed to store token: keychain: duplicate item
warning: auth OK in this shell, but next command gets 401
```

noah: ugh. seen similar when the keychain service/name changed across releases. macOS ends up with two entries and the keychain API chokes on write. can you run `security find-generic-password -s redwoodctl-token -g` to see entries?

leah: output shows two items (same account, different created-at). i tried `security delete-generic-password -s redwoodctl-token` but it only removed one and login still errors.

sam: quick safe approach: 1) logout to clear CLI cache: `redwoodctl logout --all` 2) export any profiles if you need them: `redwoodctl config export --file ~/tmp/rw-profiles.json` 3) manually delete the leftover keychain entries by GUID: run `security find-generic-password -s redwoodctl-token -g` and note the "keychain:" path + attributes, then `security delete-generic-password -s redwoodctl-token -a <your-username>` (confirm which entry)

noah: alternatively use headless auth to avoid keychain write for now: `redwoodctl login --headless --profile=local-dev` then run `redwoodctl config set profile.local-dev.store=false` to keep token in memory (temporary). But beware this loses persistence across terminal restarts.

leah: headless worked and I could finish `redwoodctl init sample-app --local`, but after restarting the terminal I got "token expired" and `redwoodctl auth refresh` produced multiple browser popups (SSO window spam) until I killed processes.

sam: that's a bug we filed last week: refresh retries don't dedupe so background retry starts another device code flow if the first hasn't completed. temp workaround: once you see the first browser window, cancel other login calls and just finish the flow. We're tracking DX-4999.

leah: any long-term fix suggestion? also worried about customers hitting this in automation (CI)

noah: two-pronged: 1) we'll add a migration shim that detects duplicate keychain items and consolidates them on upgrade (server ticket in progress). 2) for CI, always use `redwoodctl login --headless --token-file=/ci/secrets/rw.token` or set REDWOODCTL_HOME to a stable path that CI can write and use `redwoodctl login --profile=ci --headless` once to persist. we'll add docs.

devex-bot: Created ticket DX-4999: "redwoodctl: dedupe keychain entries on macOS upgrade + serialize auth refresh retries; add CI login patterns" and linked quickstart PR for headless/token-file guidance. :page_with_curl:

leah: thanks y'all. leaving steps here for others who?ll hit duplicate keychain entries. saved me a messy morning. :relieved:
